title: Three Weeks and One Short Bag
subtitle: 交通出行 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）
meta: 主题语境：交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）　|　核心词汇：mile　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 mile 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1957 the porter ① walked the mile that no visitor in the coast would have counted, and he said the walking was the whole of the week. The ② mile, meaning the distance itself and not the bag, ran three weeks and stayed uncounted in the book; a mile, he said, is the only thing in a coast that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ mile in that coast had the same short bag beside it, and the ④ mile at the far cove, meaning the ticket they kept for the children to buy and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A mile, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the porter said the counting is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the mile was the whole of the matter, meaning the journey and not the distance. The ⑥ mile, meaning the journey and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; mile, he said, is either something you walk or the only word that means both a distance and a journey. He said the journey is the part they remember.

By 1962 the ⑦ mile had become a line in a journal, and the journal had become an argument about the short bag. The ⑧ mile of the whole thing, the porter wrote in August, was one coast and three weeks of counting; mile, he said, is either the ticket at the far cove or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ mile I remember is the distance counted in the journal, which closed in 1964 and is still counted as the quietest in the coast. A ⑩ mile, my mother said in 1966, is the only distance that improves by being counted; every mile, she said, is a journey that has agreed to look like a distance. She said the journey was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 英里（指海岸里每一段旁边的那一段）
B. n. 英里（指那段英里本身，与小小的行囊相对）
C. 固定搭配：walk the mile 走这一段英里
D. n. 英里（指留给孩子们买的那一张）
E. n. 英里之事（抽象总称，指一处海岸的英里之事）
F. n. 英里（指行记里写到、被清点的那一段）
G. n. 英里、路途（指一件事里人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 路途（抽象总称，指人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: walked the mile that no visitor in the coast would have counted
The mile, meaning the distance itself and not the bag
the mile at the far cove
the mile was the whole of the matter
the mile had become a line in a journal
The mile of the whole thing
A mile, my mother said in 1966

answers.why: walk the mile 意为“走这一段英里”，1957 年那位挑夫把海岸里没有一位游客肯清点的一段英里做了一遍。
mile 意为“英里”，指那段英里本身而不是小小的行囊，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被清点。
mile 意为“英里”，指海岸里每一段旁边的那一段，每一段旁边都有同一只小小的行囊。
mile 意为“英里”，指最远那处小湾的留给孩子们买的那一张，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
mile 意为“英里、路途”，指一件事里人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这段路途就是那件事的全部。
mile 意为“路途”，指人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西而不是那段英里，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
mile 意为“英里”，指行记里写到、被清点的那一段，到 1962 年这一段成了行记里的一行。
mile 意为“英里之事”，挑夫八月写道，整件事的英里之事是一处海岸和三个星期的清点。
mile 意为“英里”，我记得的是行记里清点过的那一段，1964 年走到了，至今仍被说成海岸里最安静的一段。
mile 为抽象总称，母亲 1966 年说，英里是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的英里。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1957 年那位挑夫走了海岸里没有一位游客肯清点的一段英里，他说这一遍才是那个星期的全部。（walk the mile）
那段英里，指的是那段英里本身而不是小小的行囊，经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被清点。（mile）
那处海岸里每一段英里旁边都有同一只小小的行囊。（mile）
最远那处小湾那段英里，指的是他们留给孩子们买的那一张，是唯一有人谢过两次的。（mile）
叔叔说这段路途就是那件事的全部，指的是那样东西而不是那段英里。（mile）
1966 年母亲说，英里是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的英里。（mile）

Every mile in that coast had the same short bag beside it.
The mile at the far cove, meaning the ticket they kept for the children to buy and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice.
My uncle said the mile was the whole of the matter, meaning the journey and not the distance.
